spec.description: Retrieve information about recent deposits. Results are sorted by recency; use the `cursor` parameter to iterate through the list of deposits (page size equal to the value of `limit`) from newest to oldest. Requires the `Funds permissions - Query` API key permission.

asset.description: Filter for a specific asset being deposited.

aclass.description: Filter for a specific asset class being deposited.

method.description: Filter for a specific name of deposit method.

start.description: Start timestamp; deposits created strictly before this will not be included in the response.

end.description: End timestamp; deposits created strictly after this will not be included in the response.

cursor.description: `true`/`false` to enable/disable the paginated response shape, or a cursor string (from a previous response's `next_cursor`) to fetch the next page.

anyOf.description: Cursor for the next page of results.

limit.description: Number of results to include per page.

rebase_multiplier.description: Optional parameter for viewing xstocks data. `rebased` displays in terms of underlying equity; `base` displays in terms of SPV tokens.

anyOf.description: Deposit records, returned when `cursor` is unset or `false`.

fee.description: Fees paid. Not always present (e.g. omitted for some Ether deposits in Kraken's own documented example); type inferred as `string` by analogy with every other `fee` field in this operation family, since upstream declares no `type` for this property.

time.description: Unix timestamp when the request was made.

status.description: Status of the deposit. See the IFEX financial transaction states reference linked from upstream docs for background.

status-prop.description: Additional status property, if available: `return` for a return transaction initiated by Kraken, `onhold` when the deposit is on hold pending review.

originators.description: Sending transaction id(s), for deposits credited via a sweeping transaction.

anyOf.title: DepositStatusPage
anyOf.description: Paginated deposit results, returned when the `cursor` request parameter is set.

deposits.description: Page of deposit records. Confirmed live as `deposits` (plural) -- the endpoint's OpenAPI schema had documented this key as `deposit` (singular).

fee.description: Fees paid. Not always present (e.g. omitted for some Ether deposits in Kraken's own documented example); type inferred as `string` by analogy with every other `fee` field in this operation family, since upstream declares no `type` for this property.

time.description: Unix timestamp when the request was made.

status.description: Status of the deposit. See the IFEX financial transaction states reference linked from upstream docs for background.

status-prop.description: Additional status property, if available: `return` for a return transaction initiated by Kraken, `onhold` when the deposit is on hold pending review.

originators.description: Sending transaction id(s), for deposits credited via a sweeping transaction.

next_cursor.description: Cursor to pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page of results. `null` once there is no further page -- confirmed live.

notes: Upstream `requestBody` requires `nonce`; dropped from this schema since the core's `authed_request` (`core/transport/http.py`) injects a strictly-increasing nonce into every private call automatically -- it is never a caller-supplied parameter, matching the existing hand-written `deposit_methods(self, asset)` signature, which takes none.

No `pagination` block declared, though `cursor`/`limit`/`next_cursor` look pagination-shaped and the operation description explicitly says "use the cursor parameter to iterate through list of deposits". Two things block a clean `strategy: token` declaration: (1) the response `result` shape is itself discriminated by whether `cursor` was set on the request -- a bare array when it is omitted/false, `{deposit, next_cursor}` only once pagination is switched on -- which is exactly the "response variants discriminated by a request parameter" gap the Toolchain gaps section of docs/spec/authoring.md lists as unexpressible; (2) even granting that, `token`'s implicit "absent cursor = first page of the walk" does not hold here, since an absent cursor instead opts *out* of pagination entirely. Modeled the documented `anyOf` response shape (bare array vs `{deposit, next_cursor}`) so the schema stays accurate, but left pagination undeclared rather than force a fit; verify live (call with `cursor: true`) before a future pass tries to complete this.
